ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A car with mass $m$ starts and travels along a straight road. The engine's rated power is $P$, and the resistance encountered during the journey is constant. The maximum speed the car can reach is $v$.

1. Determine the magnitude of the resistance force acting on the car during its motion.
2. If the car starts with the rated power, find the magnitude of the instantaneous acceleration of the car when its speed is $\frac{v}{4}$.
3. If a car starts from rest with a constant acceleration, and the magnitude of the traction force is twice the magnitude of the resistance force, find the time for the car to undergo uniformly accelerated motion.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A car with mass $m$ starts and travels along a straight road. The engine's rated power is $P$, and the resistance encountered during the journey is constant. The maximum speed the car can reach is $v$. 1. Determine the magnitude of the resistance force acting on the car during its motion. 2. If the car starts with the rated power, find the magnitude of the instantaneous acceleration of the car when its speed is $\frac{v}{4}$. 3. If a car starts from rest with a constant acceleration, and the magnitude of the traction force is twice the magnitude of the resistance force, find the time for the car to undergo uniformly accelerated motion.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Read the given quantities: the car has mass m, engine rated power P, constant resistance force f, and maximum speed v. At the maximum speed, the car has zero acceleration, so the traction force balances the resistance force: F=f. Since power equals traction force times speed, at rated power and speed v we have P=fv, hence f=P/v. For the case where the car starts using rated power, when its speed is v/4, the traction force is F=P/(v/4)=4P/v. The resistance is still f=P/v, so the net force is F-f=4P/v-P/v=3P/v. Therefore the instantaneous acceleration is a=(F-f)/m=3P/(mv). For the uniformly accelerated start, the traction force is twice the resistance: F=2f. Thus the net force is 2f-f=f, so the constant acceleration is a=f/m=P/(mv). This constant-acceleration stage can continue only until the engine power needed reaches the rated power P. With traction 2f and speed u at the end of this stage, P=(2f)u, so u=P/(2f)=v/2. Since the car starts from rest, the time is t=u/a=(v/2)/(P/(mv))=mv^2/(2P).
